significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would license the form-(ii) causal conclusion that benign fine-tuning weakens refusal by perturbing "the refusal direction's supporting parameters" and that preserving this computation causally retains refusal safety at low task cost; it is not a form-(iii) scaling law or transferable quantitative relation. It establishes both a phenomenon—safety erosion during benign customization—and a compact mechanism for it, fixing which computation should be protected, but remains bounded to refusal behavior; Qi et al.'s "Fine-tuning Aligned Language Models Compromises Safety, Even When Users Do Not Intend To!" and Arditi et al.'s "Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction" show why that causal bridge would influence fine-tuning defenses. A negative result would meaningfully disfavor perturbation of the refusal subspace as the load-bearing explanation or protection target, and the true and false branches are distinguishable despite qualitative terms such as "far better" and "minimal task-performance cost." Topic substitution leaves only generic mechanism-based LLM safety, which would not earn this score; the increment is the specific causal account linking refusal-subspace preservation to durable alignment.

reach.justification: The concrete handle is a training-time "regularizer ... that penalizes changes to the model's refusal-direction computation," specifically "preserving its projection behavior on a small safety anchor set." This is ex ante rather than post hoc: it operates while a model is customized and can prevent degradation before the resulting model is deployed, giving fine-tuners and model providers an actionable control. After re-extraction on another model, the claim supplies a procedure and design rule but predicts no quantitative direction, threshold, or effect size; its asserted scope spans several classes of downstream fine-tuning, while explicitly conceding that adversarial fine-tuning and "non-refusal safety behaviors" may fall outside it. Topic substitution would remove the regularizer and its deployment-time action window and would not justify this reach; the higher band is supported specifically by an ex-ante handle usable by practitioners who customize or ship models.
